title: A finite locally free morphism of degree d carries a canonical norm of degree d compatible with base change

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite locally free morphism has a pushforward of the structure sheaf which is finite locally free of the given rank, so that after passing to a suitable affine open a basis can be chosen
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the identification of the pushforward with a free module of rank d that carries the matrix of multiplication by a section.

standard_prerequisites.name: Determinants of matrices: the determinant is independent of the chosen basis and the determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its entries
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the norm well defined and independent of the local trivialization, and gives the degree property.

standard_prerequisites.name: Over the spectrum of a field a finite dimensional algebra of dimension d admits a map to a field evaluating a vanishing section at zero, and a non-surjective endomorphism has determinant zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the vanishing criterion for the norm after base change to a field.

core_obligations: Local construction: over an affine open where the pushforward of the structure sheaf is free of rank d, choose a basis, view multiplication by a section of the structure sheaf as an endomorphism of that free module, form the associated d by d matrix over the coordinate ring, and define the norm of the section as its determinant (proof lines 3795-3803).

Well definedness and glueing: because the determinant is independent of the chosen basis the construction is well defined, so the local definitions glue to a global multiplicative map, and commutativity with base change is immediate from the construction (proof lines 3803-3808).

Properties: the first property follows because a diagonal matrix with constant entry g has determinant g to the power d, and for the second one may base change to the spectrum of a field, where a section vanishing at a point gives a non-surjective endomorphism of a finite dimensional algebra, hence determinant zero (proof lines 3810-3823).
proof_roadmap: Define the norm locally as the determinant of multiplication by a section on a local trivialization and check independence of the trivialization (proof lines 3795-3808).
Verify the degree and vanishing properties, the second after base change to a field (proof lines 3810-3823).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a canonical norm map of degree d for a finite locally free morphism and asserts its compatibility with base change (statement lines 3788-3793). The counted proof is a complete construction: over an affine chart it trivializes the pushforward, represents multiplication by a section by a matrix, defines the norm as its determinant, checks independence of the trivialization so that the local definitions glue, and then verifies the degree and vanishing properties, the latter after base change to the spectrum of a field where a vanishing section gives a non-surjective endomorphism of a finite dimensional algebra (proof lines 3795-3823). It is H2: the construction and both verifications are carried out in the counted span, with the inputs being standard linear algebra over rings.
